correctness.rationale: Exact enumeration conditioned on returns uses known Catalan weights. Lagrange inversion gives Z(n,k) and size-biased q(n,k,l); a fractional-linear adjacent-count ratio is nonincreasing with excursion length with strict distinctness at support endpoint. Independent Bernoulli signs give conditional variance A=n/4 E[L*]. Large-density limit follows from consecutive-mass recurrence and a uniform geometric bound for rho in (0,1). The actual standalone script verified 43,394 exact assertions including independently enumerated balanced walks up to 18 steps. These finite checks do not establish infinite results.

originality.rationale: The new result is a comparative likelihood-ratio ordering across EVERY prescribed return count and its strict occupation-variance consequence, rather than the already classical Catalan product law. Serlet (2014), §2 eqs.(5)–(8), explicitly contains that underlying joint enumeration; the present ratio-of-normalizers comparison (and its strong single-crossing consequence) is not among the results inspected there. Csáki–Hu and Lindell–Holst focus on ranked lengths/heights; no exact ordering was located. Further published comparison results on walk ranges, renewal models and fixed-composition runs did not state the same conditioned length ordering. Originality remains provisional to generalized renewal-allocation inequalities.
residual_risks: A general renewal-composition stochastic-order result might imply the exact finite Catalan case.

value.rationale: Prescribing the number of return excursions is a standard natural conditioning of bridges and tree/forest encodings. The new likelihood-ratio comparison orders the whole time-biased component-size law, gives strict monotonicity for every power sum of degree r>1, sharp variance endpoints n²/4 to n/4 for signed semiduration, and an explicit extensive-return asymptotic. This is not a mere isolated probability-table value; it exhibits a structural concentration law with the return count as a control parameter.
